value.rationale: A sublinear rare-type population can beat or tie a linear fast population in a many-copy collection process. The exact polynomial critical exponent plus a nonzero loglog correction, a non-Gumbel two-slope law, and a strictly nontrivial last-class probability describe the natural transition between the two extreme-value mechanisms. Such a population-size calibration is mathematically motivated by comparative defect intensities and is not a mere arbitrary finite slice.
